note: Files exempted from named agency/* rules in .oxlintrc.json, with the number of findings each exemption suppresses. The ratchet is bidirectional: a new file is red, a stale exemption is red, a changed count is red. Regenerate with `node scripts/verify/checks/lint-exempt.mjs --write` and say why in the commit.

entries.reason: THE one module allowed to do the arithmetic: bigint `*` and `/`, and the `<`/`>` that implement cmp itself. Exempting it is the premise of the whole rule set, and mirrors the four-module scoping shipped at yagoda-starter/backend/eslint.config.mjs:38-65. It deliberately KEEPS agency/no-numeric-coercion — a Number() or toFixed here is the exact hazard the module exists to prevent.

expect(['9.00','10.00'].sort()).toEqual(['10.00','9.00']) — the bare sort IS the assertion. This test pins the exact bug agency/no-implicit-sort prevents, so the rule must not be allowed to delete it.

expect([...ids].sort()).toEqual(ids) — asserts that a DEFAULT lexicographic sort reproduces createSeq's creation order, the property that makes zero-padded ids reproducible by a SQL ORDER BY id. Passing a comparator here would test the comparator, not the ids.
status >= 400 and status >= 500 — HTTP status integers chosen by the adapter itself and never read off a payload. This file JSON round-trips its response body and never inspects a domain value.
expect([...created].sort()).toEqual([...revoked].sort()) — set equality over opaque blob: URLs, where the sort IS the normalisation and no ordering claim is being made.

`${x.toFixed(2)},${y.toFixed(2)}` — SVG path coordinates, in pixels. oxlint.base.json already scopes the float and comparison rules away from **/kit/src/** as presentation, but deliberately does NOT scope no-numeric-coercion: toFixed is the money hazard itself, so it stays on everywhere and is exempted one file at a time, counted.
